Note::matrix¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

std::vector<Note> Note::matrix() const

Project Into Rows And Columns¶

matrix() decomposes a scalar, vector, or matrix into row Notes. A rank-two receiver produces one rank-one Note per row. A rank-one receiver is returned as the sole row, and a rank-zero receiver is returned as the sole scalar row. The elements therefore remain in the Note family: dtype, shape, checked typed access, and ownership are not discarded merely to expose row structure.

The promotion table is exact:

Receiver

Result

rank 0

one rank-zero Note

rank 1, shape [n]

one Note with shape [n]

rank 2, shape [r, c]

r Notes, each with shape [c]

rank 3

rejected

Only the outer std::vector and compact per-row metadata are allocated. Text rows retain the original packed byte arena; Bool, Int64, and Float64 rows retain the original aligned lane buffer and advance an offset. Thus numeric row construction is O(rows), does not copy lanes, and each row remains valid after the source Note is destroyed. Use host() when independent owning standard containers are required instead.

Empty geometry remains exact because every row is itself a Note. Shape [2, 0] becomes two Notes of shape [0]; shape [0] becomes one Note of shape [0]; shape [0, 3] produces no rows, while the source still records both extents.

Example 1: Promote A Scalar¶

const auto rows = pluss::note::make("alpha").matrix();
std::cout << "rows=" << rows.size() << " value=" << rows[0].scalar() << '\n';

Output¶

rows=1 value=alpha

Example 2: Promote A Vector To One Row¶

const auto rows = pluss::note::make({"a", "b"}).matrix();
std::cout << "rows=" << rows.size() << " shape=" << rows[0].size(0)
          << " second=" << rows[0].at(1) << '\n';

Output¶

rows=1 shape=2 second=b

Example 3: Preserve A Matrix¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        "r0c0", "r0c1", "r0c2", "r1c0", "r1c1", "r1c2"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 3}).matrix();

std::cout << "rows=" << grid.size()
          << " row-shape=" << grid[0].size(0)
          << " last=" << grid[1].at(2) << '\n';

Output¶

rows=2 row-shape=3 last=r1c2

Example 4: Distinguish Two Empty Shapes¶

const auto empty_matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 0}).matrix();
const auto empty_vector = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{0}).matrix();

std::cout << "empty rows=" << empty_matrix.size()
          << " widths=" << empty_matrix[0].numel() << ','
          << empty_matrix[1].numel() << '\n'
          << "empty vector rows=" << empty_vector.size()
          << " width=" << empty_vector[0].numel() << '\n';

Output¶

empty rows=2 widths=0,0
empty vector rows=1 width=0

Example 5: Rank Three And Absence Reject¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(
      std::vector<std::string>{"x"},
      std::array<std::int64_t, 3>{1, 1, 1}).matrix();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "matrix rank3: rejected\n";
}

try { (void)pluss::Note::undefined().matrix(); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "matrix undefined: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

matrix rank3: rejected
matrix undefined: rejected

See Also¶

  • vector: flatten any rank to one borrowed sequence.

  • slabs: extract exact three-dimensional nesting.

  • host: copy lanes into owning standard-library storage.

  • reshape: change Note geometry rather than only its C++ projection.
